newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Bandai lures investors with 'virtual pet'.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Bandai lures investors with 'virtual pet'.

text.p: Japanese toymaker Bandai Co Ltd, elated by runaway sales of a "virtual pet" toy featuring an electronic bird, is to use the craze to lure shareholders.
The firm will distribute the popular game to shareholders on its records as of March 31 in response to increasing requests, a company official told Reuters on Thursday.

Bandai, also known for its Dragon Ball and Power Ranger character toys, hopes the gift will keep shareholders loyal even after a planned October merger with Sega Enterprises Ltd, maker of the Sega Saturn 32-bit video game player,
Sales of "Tamagotchi", an chicken-like figure on a liquid crystal display that is fed and cleaned by pressing buttons, have reached nearly 1.5 million units since its debut in November.

Bandai has been hard-pressed to keep up with demand for what has become the hottest toy of 1997 even before it has gone on sale outside Japan. Shortages have led to the game changing hands at street prices of more than 20 times its retail price of 1,980 yen.
In February, police in Yokohama, south of Tokyo, took four teenage boys into custody over a suspected theft of the toy after a chase involving several patrol cars and a police helicopter.
Shareholders will receive the prized game in late June, the Bandai official said.
On the Tokyo stock market, the company shares rose 30 yen to 2,330 yen in the Thursday morning session.
Tamagotchi starts life as a bird-like image on the screen of an egg-shaped key-ring device.
It develops from chick to fully grown adult in around 10 days.
However, the owner must feed, groom and soothe the digital creature or else see it waste away and die from neglect.
